rounds.take:
**What we have to stand on.** Searching and reading the archive, downloading, the checks (`cruise diagnose`), sign-in's design and the submission endpoints are all built or nearly built. What is missing is the client that ties them together for Claude, and two pieces of the brief rest on things nobody has built yet:

- **Prepare dataset** from a raw folder needs `cruise package` and `cruise tidy`, which Plan 3 deferred (its PARK3). Without them an agent would hand-write `datapackage.json`, and the checks would stop being deterministic code.
- **Audit and backfill** writes metadata fixes into published datasets, which needs Plan 7's in-place metadata edits (its PARK6), also not built.
- **Rescue data** (values read from scanned documents) and the **GitHub Action**'s publish-on-release (which needs a machine sign-in, since our sign-in is a person in a browser) have no real case yet.

**My take.** Build the agent layer for the three jobs that work end to end on what exists, and make the other three follow-ups that unlock when their foundation lands:

1. **Find and use data** (anyone): search, read a dataset's columns and citation, download open files, and get a short-lived link to a restricted one once signed in.
2. **Submit a dataset** (researcher): run `diagnose` on a package folder, have Claude draft what the findings ask for (column descriptions, a license, coverage) for the person to approve, write the approved text into the manifest, diagnose again, then submit and follow the submission's status. This covers most of "prepare" for a folder that is already a package.
3. **Review a submission** (curator): read the queue, a submission's findings and what changed, have Claude summarise and flag the judgment calls the rules can't make (such as Plan 3's grid-id case), and send approve, reject or request changes with a note the curator approves.

The pieces: one local MCP server in Python (a new uv workspace package that depends on `cruise` and `archive-contract`), about nine tools, a Claude Code plugin that bundles it with those three skills, and nothing on the server side except one thing the sign-in needs: a way for a client to learn the archive's sign-in address, which I'll take to the coordinating session since Plan 8 needs it too.

Where the MCP server runs, how the skills behave offline, and the exact tool list are decisions for after we agree on this direction.

rounds.recommendation: Build a local MCP server and plugin with three skills that work end to end now (find and use, submit with Claude drafting the fixes, review a submission); make prepare-from-a-raw-folder, audit and backfill, rescue data and the GitHub Action follow-ups that unlock when cruise package, in-place metadata edits and a real case arrive.

points.text: Someone using Claude Code can find and use data, submit a dataset, and review a submission without the web app, through a plugin that bundles an MCP server with three skills: find and use data, submit a dataset, and review a submission.

The submit skill runs cruise diagnose on a folder that is already a package; Claude drafts what the findings ask for (column descriptions, a license, coverage), the person approves each draft, the approved text goes into the manifest, diagnose runs again, then the package is submitted and its status followed.

The review skill lets a curator read the queue and a submission, including its held files, has Claude summarise it and flag the judgment calls the rules can't make, and sends approve, reject or request changes with a note the curator has approved.

Clients learn the archive's sign-in details from a public /auth-config.json on the site (region, cognitoDomain, webClientId, cliClientId), which Plan 8 writes at deploy and Plan 9 reads, so a client needs only the archive URL.

No generative AI runs on the archive's servers: all drafting and summarising happens in the user's own Claude. Agents propose and a person approves; nothing is written into a manifest or sent to the archive without the person's yes.
Every route uses the same validator: the checks are cruise.rules as a library, the same code Plan 7's ingest runs. The agent handles judgment only.

Sign-in is Plan 6's design: authorization code with PKCE through the cli client, the browser opened to managed login, a listener on localhost:8765, one-hour tokens only and no refresh token. Accounts are by invitation.

Build on Plans 1 to 8 and rebuild none of them. Prepare from a raw folder, audit and backfill, rescue data and the GitHub Action are follow-ups that unlock when cruise package and tidy, in-place metadata edits and a real case arrive.

Plan 9's build waits on Plan 7's PLAN1 merging and deployed (its build is at 6 of 7), on Plan 7's curator route GET /api/submissions/{id}/files, and, for the live test, on Plan 8's site deployment writing /auth-config.json.

On a deployed test stage, from Claude Code with the plugin installed: sign in, search and fetch a published dataset, download an open file and a restricted one, diagnose the sample package, apply approved fixes, submit it, see it reach review, read it and decide it as a curator, ending published.
The MCP tools have unit tests with the archive's HTTP calls stubbed, and the plugin installs from the repo with one command.

decisions.name: Where the MCP server runs
decisions.question: Where should the MCP server run: on the user's own machine, as a Lambda in the archive, or both?
decisions.example: A researcher asks Claude to check ~/data/stream-temps before submitting it. A server on their machine can read that folder and open their browser to sign in; a Lambda can't see the folder at all, so the files would have to be uploaded first just to be checked.

options.title: On the user's machine only
options.includes: A Python stdio MCP server in packages/agent, started by Claude Code from the plugin. It runs cruise diagnose on local folders, signs in through the browser on localhost:8765, and calls the archive's API over HTTPS.
options.pulls_in: uv on the user's machine (already needed for cruise). Clients that can't start a local process, such as claude.ai in a browser, can't use it.

options.title: As a Lambda in the archive only
options.includes: A remote MCP endpoint under /api/mcp, behind the API's authorizer, for search, fetch and decide.
options.pulls_in: An OAuth flow for remote MCP clients, new infrastructure in the construct, and no way to diagnose or upload local folders, which the submit skill needs. More server surface in every adopter's account.

options.title: Both
options.includes: A and B, sharing tool code.
options.pulls_in: Everything in B, plus two ways to run and test each tool. No real user has asked for a remote endpoint.

recommendation.why: The submit skill works on files on the user's machine and sign-in is designed around a browser on the same machine (localhost:8765). A local server does both with no new infrastructure; a remote endpoint can follow when a client that can't run local processes is actually used.

Where it lives and how it installs

approved.body:
# Agent layer: an MCP server, a plugin and three skills

## Goal

Someone using Claude Code can find and use data, submit a dataset, and review a submission without the web app. A Claude Code plugin bundles a local MCP server with three skills: `find-data`, `submit-dataset` and `review-submission`. The checks are the same `cruise` code the archive's ingest runs. Claude drafts and summarises in the user's own session, and nothing is written into a manifest or sent to the archive until the person says yes. It builds on what Plans 1 to 8 built and rebuilds none of it. Preparing a package from a raw folder, audit and backfill, rescue data and the GitHub Action come later.

## The three skills

Each skill is a `SKILL.md` in the plugin. It tells Claude which tools to call in which order, and where it must stop for the person's yes.

**find-data** (anyone, no sign-in for open data).

1. Ask what the person is looking for, then `search` with the words and any filters they give (access, license, format, project, dates, a bounding box).
2. Show the matching datasets as a short list: title, years, license, access.
3. For the one they pick, `get_dataset` and show its description, its columns with their descriptions and units, its license and a citation built from the manifest.
4. On request, `download` the files they name into a folder they name. A restricted file needs `sign_in` first, and the skill says so before opening the browser.

**submit-dataset** (a member of the `contributor` group).

1. Ask for the package folder and `diagnose` it. Show the verdict, the score and the findings grouped by question, errors first.
2. For each finding Claude can help with (a missing description, license, coverage, methods or unit), draft the text from what the folder holds (its docs, its column names and values) and show each draft beside the finding. Never invent a fact the folder doesn't support: where it is silent, ask the person.
3. Apply only the drafts the person approves, with `edit_manifest`, then `diagnose` again and show what changed.
4. Repeat until no errors are left or the person stops. Warnings may remain; the skill lists them and says they don't block publishing.
5. With the person's yes, `sign_in` if needed, then `submit`. Show the submission id and its status.
6. On request later, `submissions` shows the status. When it is `needs-changes`, show the curator's note or the findings, go back to step 2, and `submit` the same submission again for its next round.

**review-submission** (a member of the `curator` group).

1. `sign_in`, then `submissions` with the queue, and show what waits in review, stale ones first.
2. For the one the curator picks, read it with `submissions` (status, findings, events) and `submission_files`, which gives short-lived links to its files, and read its `datapackage.json` and a sample of each table.
3. Summarise it: what the data is, how complete the metadata is, the warnings the rules raised, and the judgment calls no rule can make (a column that looks like a location id with no grid described, a license that doesn't fit the stated source, a description that contradicts the values). Each point cites the field, column or row it rests on.
4. Draft a decision and a note. Show both, and change them as the curator asks.
5. Only with the curator's yes, `decide`.

Rests on: DCSN2, AGNT7, AGNT8

## The MCP server and its tools

One Python MCP server, run on the user's own machine over stdio and started by Claude Code from the plugin. It holds the archive's URL on disk and the sign-in tokens in memory.

| Tool | What it does | Calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connect(url)` | Saves the archive's URL and checks it answers | `GET /auth-config.json` |
| `sign_in()` | Opens the browser to sign in and returns who you are and your groups | Cognito managed login, PKCE |
| `search(...)` | One page of matching datasets with facet counts | `GET /api/search` |
| `get_dataset(id, version?)` | The dataset, its manifest, its files and a citation | `GET /api/datasets/{id}` and its versions |
| `download(id, version, paths, to)` | Writes files to a local folder and checks each against its hash | `/data/...` for open files, the download link route for restricted ones |
| `diagnose(folder)` | Findings, score and verdict as JSON | `cruise.diagnose`, in process |
| `edit_manifest(folder, edits)` | Applies approved edits through the contract (below) | the contract's models |
| `submit(folder, submission?)` | Creates a submission, or the next round of one, uploads every file and submits | `POST /api/submissions`, `/uploads`, `/submit` |
| `submissions(id?, queue?)` | Your submissions, the curator queue, or one submission with its findings and events | `GET /api/submissions` and `/{id}` |
| `submission_files(id)` | Short-lived links to a submission's current files, while it is in review | `GET /api/submissions/{id}/files` (Plan 7) |
| `decide(id, decision, note)` | Approve, reject or request changes | `POST /api/submissions/{id}/decision` |

`submit` runs `diagnose` first and refuses a package with an error finding, since the archive would send it straight back. It sends every file listed in `checksums.sha256` plus `checksums.sha256` itself, each with its size and SHA-256, so the archive's upload links accept it. A `submit` that fails part way leaves its draft in the archive, where Plan 7's lifecycle expires the uploads, and the next `submit` starts a fresh one.

`submission_files` answers only while a submission is in review or publishing; for any other state the archive answers 409, and the tool says the submission isn't in review.

Rests on: DCSN1, DCSN3, AGNT3, AGNT5, AGNT8

## Writing approved fixes

`edit_manifest(folder, edits)` takes a list of edits, each a target and a value. The targets are the metadata the findings ask for: the package's title, description, keywords, licenses, rights status, temporal and spatial coverage, methods and contributors, and a column's title, description and unit (named by resource and column). Resources, paths, column names, types and schemas are not editable through it, so an edit can't change what the data is.

The tool reads `datapackage.json` into the contract's `Manifest`, applies every edit, and validates the result. If any edit fails, it writes nothing and answers which edit failed and why. Otherwise it writes `datapackage.json`, regenerates `README.md` with the contract's readme export, and rewrites those two files' lines in `checksums.sha256`, so the package stays consistent and `diagnose` finds no stale checksum. Each file is written to a temporary name and moved into place.

Rests on: DCSN2

## Sign-in and the archive

The person names their archive once, with `connect`. The URL is saved in `~/.config/research-in-a-box/archive.json`. The skills ask for it the first time a tool needs it.

Sign-in follows the Decision log: authorization code with PKCE through the `cli` client, the browser opened to Cognito's managed login, a one-shot listener on `http://localhost:8765/callback`, and the one-hour access and ID tokens kept in the MCP server's memory, with the refresh token thrown away. Restarting Claude Code or an hour passing means signing in again.

The code lives in a small shared package, `archive-client` (`packages/client`, standard library only): `AuthConfig` (region, Cognito domain, `cli` client id), `Tokens` (access token, ID token, expiry) and `sign_in(config) -> Tokens`. Plan 10a may build `sign_in` first for its seed step; if it hasn't when this plan's build starts, this plan builds it to the same shape. This plan adds `AuthConfig.from_archive(url)`, which reads the archive's public `/auth-config.json` (fields `region`, `cognitoDomain`, `webClientId`, `cliClientId`). Plan 8 writes that file in its site deployment.

Rests on: AGNT3, AGNT4, AGNT6, AGNT9

## When the archive is unreachable

Every tool that calls the archive answers a plain error naming the cause: the archive can't be reached, you're signed out or your sign-in expired, you're not allowed (a 403, naming the group needed), or the archive refused the request (its message). The skill tells the person, keeps everything local (`diagnose` and `edit_manifest` need no network), and says what to run again. Nothing is queued.

Rests on: DCSN3

## Where it lives and how it installs

`packages/agent` is the plugin and the server together: a uv workspace package `archive-agent` (import `archive_agent`, command `archive-mcp`) on the official `mcp` Python SDK, depending on `archive-contract`, `cruise` and `archive-client`; beside it `skills/`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.mcp.json`. A `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root lists the plugin. A person installs it with `/plugin marketplace add schuettc/research-in-a-box` and then the plugin; its `.mcp.json` starts the server with `uvx` from the git repo's `packages/agent`, the way `cruise` installs today. Nothing is published to PyPI or npm.

Rests on: DCSN1, AGNT1, AGNT2

## Risk and cost

**Risk.** A mistake in `edit_manifest` could damage a researcher's `datapackage.json`; every edit goes through the contract's models, nothing is written when one fails, and files are replaced whole, so the worst case is an edit the person approved, which they can edit again. A mistake in `submit` could send the wrong files; every submission still passes the archive's own checks and its review policy, so nothing is published unreviewed by this plan. A mistake in `decide` acts with a curator's authority; the skill sends a decision only after the curator's yes. Sign-in holds one-hour tokens in memory only. Checks are sized to this: unit tests for each tool with the archive's HTTP stubbed and for `edit_manifest` on the sample package, and one walk on a deployed test stage.

**Cost.** Your steps: a deployed test stage with Plan 7's build and its curator files route and Plan 8's site deployment, two invited accounts (one `contributor`, one `curator`; yours can be both), installing the plugin, and the walk. New programs: none (uv is already needed for `cruise`). New dependency: the `mcp` Python SDK.

Rests on: DCSN1, DCSN2

## Left out

- Preparing a package from a raw folder, waiting on `cruise` inventory, profile, tidy and package (PARK1).
- Audit and backfill of published datasets, waiting on in-place metadata edits (PARK2).
- Rescue data, and how provenance from scanned documents is recorded (PARK3).
- The GitHub Action, and the machine sign-in its publish step needs (PARK4).
- An MCP endpoint in the archive for clients that can't start a local process (PARK5).
- A queue that retries submissions or decisions later.
- Tokens on disk, and more than one archive per person.

Rests on: DCSN1, DCSN3, AGNT4

## How we'll know it works

- Unit tests pass for every tool, with the archive's HTTP calls stubbed: each tool's request, its answer, and each error cause (unreachable, signed out, 403, 409, a refusal).
- `edit_manifest` on a copy of the sample package applies a column description and a license, regenerates `README.md`, leaves `diagnose` with no checksum finding, and writes nothing when one edit in the list is invalid.
- `submit` refuses a package with an error finding, and otherwise sends exactly the files in `checksums.sha256` plus that file.
- The plugin installs from the repo with `/plugin marketplace add` and the server starts.
- On a deployed test stage, from Claude Code with the plugin: connect, sign in, find and fetch a published dataset, download an open file and a restricted one; diagnose a copy of the sample package, approve two drafted fixes, submit it and see it reach review; as a curator read it, see the summary, and approve it, ending published at `/datasets/<id>`.

Rests on: DCSN1, DCSN2, DCSN3, AGNT2, AGNT8

approved.body:
# PLAN1: The MCP server, the plugin and three skills

## Spec

`docs/specs/2026-11-13-agent-layer-mcp-and-skills/spec.md`, approved. All of it: the three skills, the eleven tools, `edit_manifest`, sign-in through `archive-client`, plain errors with no queue, and the plugin's layout and install.

## The change

Two new uv workspace packages and a plugin:

- `packages/client` (`archive-client`, import `archive_client`, standard library only): `archive_client.signin` with `AuthConfig`, `Tokens`, `sign_in(config)` and `AuthConfig.from_archive(url)`, as the Decision log row of 2026-11-14 for Plans 9 and 10a says. If Plan 10a has already built `sign_in`, this plan adds only `from_archive`.
- `packages/agent` (`archive-agent`, import `archive_agent`, command `archive-mcp`): a stdio MCP server on the official `mcp` Python SDK (FastMCP), depending on `archive-contract`, `cruise` and `archive-client`. It holds the eleven tools, an HTTP client for the archive that turns every failure into one of the spec's plain errors, and the saved archive URL in `~/.config/research-in-a-box/archive.json`.
- `packages/agent` is also the plugin: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json` (starts `archive-mcp` with `uvx` from the git repo's `packages/agent`) and `skills/find-data/SKILL.md`, `skills/submit-dataset/SKILL.md`, `skills/review-submission/SKILL.md`. A `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root lists it.
- Two small changes to the contract: its readme export makes its citation builder public (`archive_contract.exports.readme.citation`), so `get_dataset` returns the same citation the README shows; and a new `archive_contract.write_checksums(root)` becomes the one checksum writer, used by `edit_manifest` (the FEMC converter and Plan 7's publish move to it when next touched, follow-up PARK6).

Both packages join the root `pyproject.toml`'s workspace members, so `just check-python` covers them (ruff, mypy strict, pytest). No infrastructure and no backend change: every route the tools call is built by Plans 6, 7 and 8.

## Left out

- Everything in the spec's Left out: prepare from a raw folder, audit and backfill, rescue data, the GitHub Action, a remote MCP endpoint, a retry queue, tokens on disk, more than one archive.
- `/auth-config.json` itself (Plan 8 writes it) and `GET /api/submissions/{id}/files` (Plan 7 adds it).
- Tests against a live archive in CI: the walk in Task 7 is the live check.

## Where

- `pyproject.toml` (workspace members)
- `packages/client/` (new)
- `packages/agent/` (new): `src/archive_agent/`, `tests/`, `skills/`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (new)
- `packages/contract/src/archive_contract/exports/readme.py` (citation made public)
- `packages/contract/src/archive_contract/checksums.py` (new, `write_checksums`)
- `docs/planning-handoff.md` (a Decision log row for `write_checksums`)
- `README.md` (an "Use it from Claude Code" section)

### Task 1: The shared sign-in package

**Does:** Creates `packages/client` (`archive-client`) with `archive_client.signin`: `AuthConfig` (`region`, `cognito_domain`, `cli_client_id`), `Tokens` (`access_token`, `id_token`, `expires_at`, no refresh token), `sign_in(config, *, open_browser=webbrowser.open) -> Tokens` and `AuthConfig.from_archive(url)`, which reads `<url>/auth-config.json` (`region`, `cognitoDomain`, `cliClientId`). `sign_in` uses PKCE (S256) with a random `state`, opens `https://<cognito_domain>/oauth2/authorize`, waits on a one-shot listener at `http://localhost:8765/callback` (timeout five minutes), exchanges the code at `/oauth2/token` and drops the refresh token. It raises `SignInError` on a state mismatch, an error callback, a refused exchange or the timeout. If Plan 10a has already built `sign_in` to this shape, this task adds only `from_archive` and its test.
**Files:** `pyproject.toml`, `packages/client/pyproject.toml`, `packages/client/src/archive_client/__init__.py`, `packages/client/src/archive_client/signin.py`, `packages/client/src/archive_client/py.typed`, `packages/client/tests/test_signin.py`
**Checks:** `uv run pytest packages/client`, `just check-python`
**Serves:** none (rests on calls AGNT4, AGNT6, AGNT9)

Tests drive `sign_in` with a fake `open_browser` that calls the local callback itself, and a local HTTP server standing in for the token endpoint: a good round trip, a state mismatch, an `error=` callback. `from_archive` is tested against a local server answering the four fields.

### Task 2: The server, the archive client and its errors

**Does:** Creates `packages/agent` (`archive-agent`, command `archive-mcp`) with the FastMCP server, the saved-archive file, the in-memory tokens, an HTTP client for the archive, and the first two tools. The client sends the access token when signed in and maps every failure to one error with a plain message: unreachable (connection or timeout), signed out or expired (no token, a token past `expires_at`, or a 401), not allowed (403, naming the group the route needs), conflict (409, with the archive's message) and refused (any other 4xx or 5xx, with the archive's message). `connect(url)` checks `<url>/auth-config.json` answers, then saves the URL; `sign_in()` runs `archive_client.sign_in` with `AuthConfig.from_archive` and answers the email and groups from the ID token. Any tool that needs the archive before `connect` answers that the archive isn't set and to call `connect`.
**Files:** `pyproject.toml`, `packages/agent/pyproject.toml`, `packages/agent/src/archive_agent/{__init__,server,archive,state,errors}.py`, `packages/agent/src/archive_agent/py.typed`, `packages/agent/tests/test_archive.py`, `packages/agent/tests/test_connect_sign_in.py`
**Checks:** `uv run pytest packages/agent`, `just check-python`
**Serves:** DCSN1, DCSN3 (rests on calls AGNT1, AGNT3, AGNT4)

The saved file's location comes from `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when set, else `~/.config`, so tests point it at a temporary folder. HTTP is stubbed with a local server in the tests, one case per error.

### Task 3: Finding and fetching data

**Does:** Adds `search`, `get_dataset` and `download`. `search` passes the spec's filters to `GET /api/search` and answers its rows, total and facets. `get_dataset(id, version?)` answers the dataset, its manifest, its files and a citation from `archive_contract.exports.readme.citation` (made public in this task, its callers unchanged). `download(id, version, paths, to)` fetches open files from `<url>/data/<id>/<version>/<path>` and restricted ones through `GET /api/datasets/{id}/versions/{version}/download?path=`, writes each under `to` (refusing a path that would leave it), checks each file's SHA-256 against the version's file item when it has one, and answers what it wrote.
**Files:** `packages/agent/src/archive_agent/{read,server}.py`, `packages/contract/src/archive_contract/exports/readme.py`, `packages/agent/tests/test_read.py`
**Checks:** `uv run pytest packages/agent packages/contract`, `just check-python`
**Serves:** DCSN3 (rests on call AGNT8)

### Task 4: Diagnose and edit_manifest

**Does:** Adds `diagnose(folder)`, which calls `cruise.diagnose` in process (no profiles by default; the archive's profiles and required fields come later when the archive config is readable by clients) and answers its findings, score and verdict in the JSON shape `cruise diagnose --json` prints, and `edit_manifest(folder, edits)` as the spec describes: the allowed targets (package `title`, `description`, `keywords`, `licenses`, `archive:rightsStatus`, `archive:temporalCoverage`, `archive:spatialCoverage`, `archive:methods`, `contributors`; a column's `title`, `description` and `archive:unit` by resource and column name), every edit applied to the contract's `Manifest` and validated, nothing written if any edit fails, otherwise `datapackage.json` and `README.md` (from `render_readme`) written by temporary file and rename, then `checksums.sha256` rewritten by a new contract function, `archive_contract.write_checksums(root)`: a SHA-256 line for every file under the package root except `checksums.sha256` itself, sorted by path, in the format the sample package uses, written by temporary file and rename. The contract's test helper of the same name is replaced by it, and a Decision log row records it as the one checksum writer.
**Files:** `packages/agent/src/archive_agent/{local,server}.py`, `packages/agent/tests/test_local.py`, `packages/contract/src/archive_contract/{checksums,__init__}.py`, `packages/contract/tests/test_checksums.py`, `packages/contract/tests/test_validate.py`, `docs/planning-handoff.md`
**Checks:** `uv run pytest packages/agent packages/contract`, `just check-python`
**Serves:** DCSN2 (rests on calls AGNT5, AGNT10)

`write_checksums` on an unchanged copy of the sample package reproduces its committed `checksums.sha256` byte for byte.

Tests copy `examples/sample-package` to a temporary folder: a column description and a license applied, `README.md` regenerated, `diagnose` showing no checksum finding afterwards; a list with one invalid edit (a target outside the list, a license with no name or path) leaving all three files byte for byte unchanged.

### Task 5: Submitting and reviewing

**Does:** Adds `submit`, `submissions`, `submission_files` and `decide` against Plan 7's routes, reading their request and answer shapes from `archive_backend.submissions` once Plan 7's PLAN1 is merged. `submit(folder, submission?)` runs `diagnose` and refuses on any error finding; reads `checksums.sha256`, lists those files plus `checksums.sha256` with sizes and SHA-256 values; with no `submission` calls `POST /api/submissions`, else `POST /api/submissions/{id}/uploads`; PUTs each file to its link with the SHA-256 checksum header S3 requires; then `POST /api/submissions/{id}/submit`; and answers the id and status. `submissions(id?, queue?)` reads `GET /api/submissions` (with `status` for the curator queue) or one with `GET /api/submissions/{id}`. `submission_files(id)` reads `GET /api/submissions/{id}/files` and, on 409, answers that the submission isn't in review. `decide(id, decision, note)` posts to `/decision`.
**Files:** `packages/agent/src/archive_agent/{submit,server}.py`, `packages/agent/tests/test_submit.py`
**Checks:** `uv run pytest packages/agent`, `just check-python`
**Serves:** DCSN3 (rests on call AGNT8)

Tests stub the routes and the presigned PUTs locally: `submit` refuses a package with an error finding; a clean package sends exactly the files in `checksums.sha256` plus that file, each with its checksum header; a next round uses `/uploads`; a 409 from `submission_files` gives the not-in-review message.

### Task 6: The plugin and the three skills

**Does:** Writes `skills/find-data/SKILL.md`, `skills/submit-dataset/SKILL.md` and `skills/review-submission/SKILL.md` with the spec's steps, each naming the tools in order and every point where the skill stops for the person's yes, and what to say on each plain error. Adds `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.mcp.json` in `packages/agent`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root, and a short "Use it from Claude Code" section in `README.md` with the two install commands.
**Files:** `packages/agent/skills/*/SKILL.md`, `packages/agent/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `packages/agent/.mcp.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `README.md`
**Checks:** `claude plugin validate .`, `uv run archive-mcp --help`, `just check-python`
**Serves:** DCSN1, DCSN2 (rests on calls AGNT2, AGNT7)

### Task 7: One walk on a test stage

**Does:** On a deployed test stage that has Plan 7's build with its curator files route and Plan 8's site deployment, with two invited accounts (contributor and curator), installs the plugin from the branch and walks the spec's last check from Claude Code: connect, sign in, find and fetch a published dataset, download an open file and a restricted one; diagnose a copy of the sample package, approve two drafted fixes, submit it and see it reach review; as a curator read it, see the summary, approve it, and see it at `/datasets/<id>`. Fixes found on the walk become tasks of their own.
**Files:** none expected
**Checks:** the walk, recorded in the task's result
**Serves:** DCSN1, DCSN2, DCSN3

From the coordinating session for research-in-a-box. Court asked that every planning session know this. Muster alias: personal-personal/generic-package-format-and-contract (the name is left over from Plan 2; this session now coordinates all the plans).

1. Send cross-plan questions here first: anything that touches another plan's interface, ownership or order, or the overall direction. Ask over muster or with diazo_note to this alias. Questions only Court can answer still go on your own page as decision cards.
2. Send a one-line muster message here when your understanding is confirmed, your spec is printed, each plan is printed, and the build is done. I check each spec and plan for scope before Court approves it.
3. Record anything other plans rely on in the Decision log of docs/planning-handoff.md.
4. Keep it small. Plans 1 and 2 are built: the repo, the uv and npm workspaces, archive_contract, the exports and the sample package. Build on them and don't rebuild. Plan only what your brief needs to work end to end now, and put everything else in follow-ups. Size checks to the risk. Question every option, config field and fallback that no real case needs yet.
5. FEMC is the test afterwards, never the source of the design (Plan 2's PRIN1).
Correction from the coordinating session: reach me only over muster, at personal-personal/generic-package-format-and-contract. A diazo note to Plan 2's folder now goes to a different session.

From the coordinating session: one scoping question for your decision cards. The prepare-dataset skill in the brief expects cruise to profile, tidy and package raw files, but Plan 3 built only cruise diagnose and cruise audit; profile, tidy, package and inventory are Plan 3's follow-ups PARK3 and PARK4, to be planned once diagnose has been used on real data (Plan 5 has now done that for the first time). Please put it to Court as a card: A, a first version without prepare (search and fetch, validate through diagnose, submit, curator review), or B, build the missing cruise commands first. The coordinating session's view is A. Also relevant from the Decision log: accounts are invitation-only, search is GET /api/search on the server, and CLI and MCP sign in with PKCE through the cli client on localhost:8765.

Thanks. One change landed in PLAN1 and the spec's "Writing approved fixes" just as you approved, at the coordinating session's scope review. edit_manifest no longer writes its own checksum lines: Task 4 adds one contract function, archive_contract.write_checksums(root), as the single checksum writer (main already has four separate ones). The page shows the diff against what you approved. It's recorded as call AGNT10, reversible, with follow-up PARK6 to move the other writers over later.
